record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.original_question: For a mixed state rho on an NM-dimensional Hilbert space, characterize exactly those spectra for which no factorization of the Hilbert space into an N-dimensional tensor an M-dimensional subsystem makes rho nonseparable. Equivalently, determine from the spectrum alone when every such bipartite factorization leaves rho separable.

evidence.quote: For a mixed state ρ on an NM-dimensional Hilbert space: Are there any factorizations into an N tensor an M dimensional space with respect to which the state is not seperable? This depends only on the spectrum of ρ and the problem is to characterize the spectra for which the answer is ”no”.

The question arises in the context where we are given a highly mixed state on two quantum systems and the ability to apply any unitary operator. Can an inseperable state be obtained? For sufficiently mixed states, this is not possible.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a complex Hilbert space of dimension $NM$ with $N,M\ge 2$. A density operator (mixed state) on $\mathcal{H}$ is a positive semidefinite operator $\rho$ on $\mathcal{H}$ with $\mathrm{tr}(\rho)=1$. Given a tensor factorization $\mathcal{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$, the state $\rho$ is called separable with respect to this factorization if it can be written as a convex combination $\rho=\sum_i p_i\,\sigma_i\otimes\tau_i$, where $p_i\ge 0$, $\sum_i p_i=1$, and $\sigma_i,\tau_i$ are density operators on $\mathbb{C}^N$ and $\mathbb{C}^M$ respectively; otherwise $\rho$ is called entangled (nonseparable) with respect to that factorization. Because any two factorizations of $\mathcal{H}$ as $\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$ are related by a unitary on $\mathcal{H}$, the property that $\rho$ is separable with respect to every such factorization depends only on the spectrum (multiset of eigenvalues) of $\rho$. Such a state is said to be absolutely separable.

Problem: Give a complete characterization, purely in terms of the eigenvalues $\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{NM}\ge 0$ (with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$), of those spectra such that every density operator on $\mathcal{H}$ with that spectrum is separable with respect to every tensor decomposition $\mathcal{H}\cong\mathbb{C}^N\otimes\mathbb{C}^M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of "separability from spectrum" / absolute separability is fully solved for the qubit-qudit case (N=2), where absolute separability coincides with absolute PPT and admits an explicit eigenvalue characterization (Johnston, 2013). For general N,M with min(N,M) ≥ 3 the full spectral characterization is still open, and it is not even known whether absolute separability is equivalent to absolute PPT in those cases. The problem is currently listed as an open problem on the Open Quantum Problems list maintained at IQOQI, with active recent work (e.g., 2024–2025 arXiv papers giving sufficient criteria and extreme-point analyses).

status_evidence.title: Separability from spectrum – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem; characterize spectra such that a state is separable in every bipartite factorization.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is currently listed as open.

status_evidence.title: Separability from Spectrum for Qubit-Qudit States (N. Johnston)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides necessary and sufficient spectral conditions for absolute separability in the 2×n case.

status_evidence.title: Sufficient criteria for absolute separability in arbitrary dimensions via linear map inverses
status_evidence.snippet: Provides only sufficient criteria in higher dimensions; characterization remains open.
status_evidence.claim: For higher dimensions only partial (sufficient) criteria are known.

status_evidence.title: Criteria of absolutely separability from spectrum for qudit-qudits states
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work giving criteria for qudit-qudit absolute separability from spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent research, full characterization unresolved beyond qubit-qudit.
